Definition: from G4862 and G2346; to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides:--throng.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus goes with Jairus, and much people follow Him and throng Him, and the disciples say, You see the multitude thronging You, and You say, Who touched Me? The crowd presses on every side, and in the middle of the pressing one touch of faith draws power out of Him.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that a thronging crowd cannot stop one touch of faith, and I hold that my touch, like the woman's, is what Jesus feels.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
